answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud or duplicated claims. A trellis of review links can route each claim to randomly selected, stake-bearing peers, while yarrow and basalt serve as ordinary task labels, not identity proofs. Creating a thousand sybils then means buying and immobilizing a thousand stakes; coordinating them also risks forfeiture, making the attack costly rather than merely a matter of minting accounts.
